rows: Morgan Stanley Global Consumer & Retail Conference 2021

Management reiterated the bull case: a 'new age' functional energy drink, science-backed (six-plus published clinical studies), differentiated by seven essential vitamins, green tea/guarana/ginger, no sugar, 'no crash, no jitters.'

Celsius is 'back-dooring' the energy category - built from gym/specialty roots into grocery, mass, drug and Amazon (18% share, #2 on Amazon, recently past Red Bull) - now attacking convenience as the DSD network activates.

Growth algorithm framed as three pillars: new distribution (total ACV only ~34%), optimization of existing distribution (cold/warm/secondary placement, 900+ coolers), and an innovation pipeline (Strawberry Guava, Fuji Apple Pear, the Vibe sub-line, an upcoming summer Vibe).
Clearest headwind: a supply-chain 'perfect storm' - ~7% Q3 gross-profit/COGS impact labeled transitory (~3% freight inefficiency, ~4% imported can costs).
Expects to cycle through ~600 containers of pre-paid international cans by mid-year 2022; US can supply secured for 2022; ~3% freight reducible via the six-orbit model.
COGS includes inbound freight, so a normalized pro forma gross margin is closer to ~50%; margin impact expected to persist several quarters.
DSD 80% long-term target reflects that most traditional retail will be DSD-serviced while a portion (health/fitness, retailers with own supply chains) will not.
Hard-seltzer slowdown freed AB-distributor focus for Celsius and made US cans available on the spot market; Celsius explicitly ruled out hard seltzer.
Category-wide ~$0.25/can price increases via promotional optimization rather than frontline list pricing; Celsius following the same approach.

Organically created sub-lines (CELSIUS HEAT, BCAA recovery) available to bring to mainstream retail 'at the right time'; also exploring hydration and protein adjacencies; FAST protein-snack portfolio on a small base sold on Amazon.
M&A: 'not actively looking' but would evaluate accretive bolt-ons; the national DSD network, once optimized, enables future addition of other brands on the same route to market.

International uses an asset-light master-distributor model invoicing in USD; recently launched on Amazon in the UK, Germany and South Korea; broad opportunity in Europe and Asia, but the clear emphasis is the US.
Demographic expansion (Gen Z entering at higher per-cap rates) and COVID-magnified health-and-wellness trends seen as durable category tailwinds.
Tone emphatically bullish; management stressed staying focused on the core portfolio and not getting distracted.
What are the largest drivers of momentum in the energy drink space and the key drivers of future growth?

The category has been a top beverage growth driver for over a decade as people work more/harder and want more energy. COVID-driven health-and-wellness and functional-fitness trends drive emphasis toward the category; Celsius delivers seven essential vitamins, green tea, ginger and guarana without sacrificing flavor, plus functionality. Cited a category CAGR over 6% to 2025, demographic expansion, and higher per-cap consumption among new (Gen Z) consumers.
With increasing competition, how is Celsius positioned to stand out and differentiate from peers?

Celsius is one of the only science-backed products - six-plus published clinical studies, the basis of structure/function claims - making it a proven functional energy drink ('Energy 2.0') difficult to replicate. Low barriers to entry but high barriers to stay. CFO cited the green-tea/guarana/ginger ingredient set and the 'no crash, no jitters' sustained-energy experience driving high continuity.
How does management think about the Celsius sales growth algorithm - same-store sales, new distribution, e-commerce, innovation?

Three pillars: (1) new distribution - total ACV only ~34%, 'back-dooring' into convenience as DSD activates; (2) optimizing existing distribution - cold/warm/secondary placement, 900+ coolers placed with more in 2022; (3) the innovation pipeline - Strawberry Guava, Fuji Apple Pear, the Vibe sub-line and a new summer Vibe. CFO stressed DSD 'white glove' execution exponentially drives incremental sales.
Talk about the publicly announced 80% long-term DSD distribution target - strategy, implementation, and why 80%.

80% reflects that most traditional retail will be DSD-serviced, while a portion (health/fitness channel, retailers with their own supply chains) will not. Conversion is region-by-region, retailer-by-retailer: Target ~95% converted, Walmart converted, CVS and 7-Eleven in progress. CFO added the back-office work makes it 'a journey, not flipping a switch.' Distributors up over 300% in Q2/Q3.
Any interesting adjacencies, given the stated lack of interest in hard seltzer - what other beverage sub-sectors are interesting?

Stay focused on the core portfolio, but organically created sub-lines are available to bring to mainstream retail at the right time - CELSIUS HEAT and the BCAA recovery line - plus exploration of hydration and protein opportunities and the FAST protein-snack portfolio. Methodical resource allocation; opportunities evaluated if accretive.
How have supply-chain headwinds and cost inflation affected the company, given the margin impact in the latest earnings release?

CFO described a 'perfect storm' - freight, container costs, storage, re-works - plus the six-orbit warehouse transition. CEO quantified ~7% of Q3 gross profit/COGS as transitory: ~3% freight inefficiency (reducible ~3% via orbit optimization) and ~4% imported can costs. Pre-paid for ~600 containers of international cans (ordered February), cycling through by mid-2022; US cans secured for 2022. COGS includes inbound freight, so normalized pro forma gross margin is ~50%.
How does management think about price in the current environment - any comments on pricing strategy?

Everyone is effectively taking price through promotional optimization without raising frontline list prices - observed two-can deals moving up roughly $0.25/can. Celsius, like Red Bull and Monster, has not taken frontline pricing but has worked its promotional strategies; has pricing strategies in place and is monitoring closely.
How does the company think about M&A - new geographies, categories or otherwise?

'Not actively looking' but would evaluate an accretive bolt-on that fits its synergies, while stressing focus on the massive US opportunity. The national DSD network, once optimized, enables future addition of other brands on the same route to market. CFO reiterated the international master-distributor model (USD revenue, limited footprint), with clear US emphasis.
Update on the Amazon relationship including the recent Amazon Europe launch, plus general commentary on geographic focus.

Called Amazon 'phenomenal' - an 18% US share, #2 energy drink, recently past Red Bull. The loyal consumer buying a warm 12-pack for $25-30 to chill at home excites management; against a ~2% Nielsen tracked-channel share, that signals the runway. Amazon is growing internationally; Celsius recently launched on Amazon in the UK, Germany and South Korea (plus the FAST portfolio online), with COVID-impacted opportunity in Malaysia. CFO said the international Amazon launches fit the asset-light model.
